catalog_crop_carrot: The carrot is the root of a plant in the parsley family; the orange kind was bred in the Netherlands in the seventeenth century. It is a starter crop: of the crops grown on plots, it ripens the soonest and stays happy with the widest range of water and fertilizer, and its seed is among the cheapest. It also sells for the least, so plant crops that sell for more once you can.
catalog_crop_potato: A potato is not a root but a swollen underground stem, first farmed in the Andes of South America. It is a starter crop: it ripens sooner than most crops, uses less water than most, and stays fresh longer than most. It sells for little as fruit; a Pot still distills it into Vodka.
catalog_crop_wheat: Wheat is a grass, and one of the first plants people farmed, in the Middle East about ten thousand years ago. It sells for more than the starter crops, and it is grown for machines: the Mill crushes it into Flour, a Furnace bakes Flour into Bread, and a Pot still distills it into Beer.
catalog_crop_tomato: Botanically a tomato is a berry, and for a long time Europeans grew it only for its looks, believing it was poisonous. It uses more water than most crops and loses freshness faster than most once ripe, so harvest and sell it soon, or make it into Ketchup in the Jam machine.
catalog_crop_raspberry: A raspberry is dozens of tiny fruits, each around its own seed, grown on a cane of the rose family. As fruit it sells for as much as any crop, but it loses freshness faster than any other: sell it soon after harvest, or make it into jam in the Jam machine.
catalog_crop_apple: Apples come from the wild apple forests of Central Asia. An apple seed does not grow into the same kind of apple as its parent, so every named apple is grown from grafts. Of the tree fruits, the apple stays fresh the longest, and a Barrel ages it into Cider.
catalog_crop_grape: People have made wine from grapes for about eight thousand years. Grapes sell well as fruit but lose freshness faster than most crops; the Jam machine makes jam from them, and a Barrel ages them into Wine.
catalog_crop_vanilla: Vanilla is the only orchid grown for food. Each flower opens for a single day, and on most farms it is pollinated by hand. Of the crops grown on plots, it ripens the slowest, its seed costs the most, and it stays happy in the narrowest range of water and fertilizer. The Mill crushes it into Vanilla extract, which the Infuser uses to infuse goods.
catalog_crop_chilli: The heat of a chilli comes from capsaicin, which mammals feel and birds do not, so birds eat chillies and spread their seeds. Of the crops grown on plots, it uses the least water and the most fertilizer, and it stays fresh the longest. The Mill crushes it into Flakes, which the Infuser uses to infuse goods.
catalog_crop_sugar_cane: Sugar cane is a tall grass that stores sugar in its stems; most of the world's sugar is made from it. As fruit it sells for little, and it uses more water than any other crop. Grow it for the Mill, which crushes it into Sugar for the Jam machine or the Market.
catalog_crop_apricot: The apricot is named after Armenia, where the Romans thought it came from. It gives its first fruit sooner than any other tree and stays happy with more or less water and fertilizer than any other tree. It sells for little as fruit; the Jam machine makes jam from it, and a Pot still distills it into Brandy.
catalog_crop_olive: Olive trees can live for more than a thousand years, and people pressed olives for oil before they could write. It takes longer than any other tree to give its first fruit, and uses the least water of the trees. Olives sell for the most of the tree fruits, and the Mill crushes them into Olive oil.
catalog_crop_cherry: Most sweet cherry trees cannot pollinate their own flowers; bees have to bring pollen from another cherry tree nearby. It gives fruit more often than any other tree, but its fruit sells for the least of the tree fruits and loses freshness the fastest: pick it up soon and sell it, or make it into jam in the Jam machine.
catalog_shovel: Digs grass and hard soil, and uproots plants and shrubs. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per dig.
catalog_better_shovel: Digs everything a Shovel digs, faster than a Shovel and for more uses. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per dig.
catalog_pickaxe: Breaks rocks and very hard soil. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per mine.
catalog_better_pickaxe: Breaks rocks and very hard soil faster than a Pickaxe, and for more uses. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per mine.
catalog_bucket: Holds {n} L. Fill at a pump or well. {plot} L fills one plot.
catalog_weed_spray: Holds {n} L. Click tilled soil to starve weeds there.
catalog_pumpjack: Gathers {rate} L/day into a {cap} L tank. Fill a bucket straight from it, or run pipe out of any of its corners to feed taps and sprinklers. Litres it pumps are billed as Water at the end of the day.
catalog_chest: {n} slots. Walk up and store any item.
catalog_grinder: Hopper. One fruit becomes {min}–{max} seeds of the same crop and rarity. {workSeconds}s per fruit.
catalog_pipe: Lies on the edge between two tiles and carries water from a source to your taps and sprinklers. Drag while placing to lay a whole run at once. Any pipe touching a source at a corner is fed by it.
catalog_sprinkler: Waters a {w}×{h} area of plots, {day} L a day each. It pours only on plots with something growing, and only while pipe connects it to a source that still holds water.
catalog_sprinkler_vert: Waters a {w}×{h} strip, {day} L a day per plot. Rotate it while placing to lay the strip north-south or east-west.
catalog_sprinkler_large: Waters a {w}×{h} area, {day} L a day per plot.
catalog_well: Gathers {rate} L/day into a {cap} L tank. Litres you draw are not billed as Water, unlike a Pump. Fill a bucket straight from it, or run pipe out of any of its corners to feed taps and sprinklers. A Drought gathers more slowly than Clear, Rain, Dry, or Flood.
catalog_valve: Sits on one pipe, and lays that pipe too if the edge is bare. Click it and the gardener walks over to shut that pipe off, or open it again. Water still reaches a sprinkler by any other open route.
catalog_tap: Fills a bucket at {rate} L/s, as long as pipe connects it to a source. Put one next to your tilled soil and you stop walking back to the pump. Once the tanks run dry it fills only as fast as your sources make water.
catalog_hangar: {w}×{h} industrial shed. Buy Quads and tractors at a hangar.
catalog_refuel: Makes fuel in a batch of {batch} L, once {batch} units are in and it holds none. A route takes that fuel on the south side. Buy from market pays for the liters it is not holding, when you can pay for all of them.
catalog_silo_seed: A seed store for vehicles. A Tractor with a Seeder loads seeds here at the loading spots above and below the silo. It holds up to {cap} seeds; open it to buy seed packs into it, as at the Seed silo. With Auto-restock on, it buys back each pack a vehicle takes while you have the money. Named and Heirloom seeds are not restocked.
catalog_silo_spray: A fertilizer store for vehicles. A Tractor with a Sprayer loads fertilizer or compost here at the loading spots above and below the silo. It holds up to {cap} L of fertilizer, compost, Weed spray and sugar; open it to buy bags into it, as at the Additive store. With Auto-restock on, it buys back each bag a vehicle takes while you have the money.
catalog_silo_produce: A harvest store for vehicles. A Tractor with a Harvester unloads fruit, Pulled weed and Cut grass here at the loading spots above and below the silo. It has {slots} slots; open it to take the harvest out, as from a Chest.
catalog_lever: A switch you flip by hand with Flip lever. It stays where you leave it, so whatever is wired to it stays on or off until someone flips it back.
catalog_button: A button you press with Press button. It sends one short signal per press. Wire it to a Lever's input to flip that Lever from where the button is.
catalog_lamp: A light that shows whether a wire carries a signal. It does nothing else; place one beside your wiring to see what the wiring is doing.
catalog_or: Turns on when either of its two inputs is on.
catalog_and: Turns on only while both of its inputs are on.
catalog_logic: Combines two signals into one. Tune it to OR when either signal should be enough, or to AND when both are needed, for example a Sprinkler that pours only at Sunrise and only while a plant is wilting.
catalog_not: Turns a signal around: off becomes on, and on becomes off. Use it when something should run while a sensor is off, for example a Sprinkler that pours on every day without Rain.
catalog_pulser: Turns a signal that stays on into one short signal. Put it in front of a Counter so each time a signal turns on counts once, however long it stays on.
catalog_counter: Counts its input and sends one signal each time the count reaches a number you set. With a Pulser in front of it, it counts how many times a signal has turned on, for example every third time a vehicle arrives at a Pressure plate.
catalog_sensor_water: Watches the plants and trees around it and sends a signal while any of them is wilting or drowning. Wire it to a Sprinkler with only Wilting ticked, and the sprinkler pours only while a plant is wilting.
catalog_sensor_fert: Watches the growing plants and trees around it and sends a signal while any of them is starving for fertilizer. Wire it to a Vehicle dispatcher to send a Sprayer out when a field needs fertilizer.
catalog_sensor_harvest: Watches the crops around it and sends a signal when they are ready to harvest. Wire it to a Vehicle dispatcher to send a Harvester out when the crops are ripe.
catalog_sensor_day: Sends a signal during the parts of the day you tick, so whatever is wired to it runs at a set part of every day.
catalog_sensor_variety: Watches the plants and trees around it and sends a signal while one of them is Plain, Named or Heirloom, as you tick. Use it to spot a plant that has turned into a Named or Heirloom Variety before it is harvested with the rest.
catalog_sensor_weather: Sends a signal all day on days with the weather you tick. Wire it through a NOT gate to a Sprinkler to keep the sprinkler off on days of Rain.
catalog_water_system: Joins your water network like a tap, and turns on when the sprinklers want more water than the tanks hold. Wire it to a valve to shut part of the field off before the whole network runs dry.
catalog_vehicle_detector: Sends a signal while something you tick is on it or next to it: a vehicle, a gardener, or an item on the ground. Use it to react when a vehicle arrives, or to notice fruit that has dropped from a tree nearby.
catalog_dispatch: Sends one vehicle out on a route when its signal rises. The signal stays on while at least that many vehicles are out on the route.
catalog_traffic_light: Stops a vehicle on its route while its input is off, and lets it go when the input turns on. It sends a signal of its own while a vehicle is waiting, so one vehicle can wait for another to finish.
catalog_sku_pack: Pack of {n} {name} seeds. Plant on tilled soil.
catalog_sku_pack_sugar_cane: Pack of {n} {name} seeds. Plant on tilled soil. Ripe cane is fruit. Mill cane for sugar.
catalog_sku_pack_grass: Pack of {n}. Sow on tilled soil. Drinks almost nothing and takes a quarter day to root, then the plot goes back to untilled lawn.
catalog_sku_buy_fertilizer: Holds {n} L. Tops a plot back up to full fertilizer, spending only what the soil is missing.
catalog_sku_buy_compost_box: Drop organic waste in. {need} units make {liters} L of compost in {seconds}s. A chest on the right takes the bag, else it drops beside the box.
catalog_sku_buy_fence: Sits in the middle of an untilled tile and joins up with the fences beside it. Marks a boundary; the gardener still walks through.
catalog_sku_buy_tile: Paving. Lays on untilled ground and stays put. Keeps the garden walkable and tidy.
catalog_sku_buy_mill: Hopper mill. {cane} cane crushes in {work}s, {cane} olive in {olive}s, {cane} wheat in {wheat}s, and {grass} grass in {grassWork}s. Cane makes {bag} L sugar at {sale}/L.
catalog_sku_buy_jam: {fruit} fruit and sugar cook in {seconds}s. Ketchup takes twice the sugar a jam does, and Passata takes none. Holds {buffer} L of sugar.
catalog_sku_buy_still: Distills {cap} potato, wheat or apricot with {water} L water in {seconds}s.
catalog_sku_buy_barrel: Five grapes or four apples. Matures in {mature}s, ages to {age}s.
catalog_sku_buy_freezer: {n} slots. Fruit in here rots {pct}% slower.
catalog_sku_buy_freezer_large: {n} slots. Fruit in here rots {pct}% slower. Earned from a contract, never sold.
catalog_fertilizer: Holds {n} L. Tops a plot back up to full fertilizer, spending only what the soil is missing. Empty bags are thrown away.
catalog_compost: Holds {liters} L. Tops a plot back up to full fertilizer, spending only what the soil is missing.
catalog_compost_box: Drop any organic waste in. {need} units become {liters} L of compost in {seconds}s. A chest on the right takes the bag, else it drops beside the box. Seeds {seeds}, fruit {fruit}, heirloom fruit {heirloom}, rotten fruit {rotten}, dead plants and weeds {dead}.
catalog_soil: Tilled soil holds water and fertilizer, and keeps them through planting, harvest and death. Water reads {min} to {max} L; plants want {mid} L and drown above it. Fertilizer runs from {fertMin} to {fertMax} and a growing plant empties a full plot in three days.
catalog_weed: Takes over tilled soil left without seed. Full grown in {seconds}s and drinks water and fertilizer the whole time. Dig it out with a shovel.

match.nPlural=one: What is left when a plant drowns or a ripe crop is never picked. After Fermentation, Drop off at the Market. Worth {n} unit in the Compost box.
match.nPlural=other: What is left when a plant drowns or a ripe crop is never picked. After Fermentation, Drop off at the Market. Worth {n} units in the Compost box.

match.nPlural=one: What is left when a plant dries out or starves. Worth nothing at market, worth {n} unit in the compost box.
match.nPlural=other: What is left when a plant dries out or starves. Worth nothing at market, worth {n} units in the compost box.

match.nPlural=one: Cut from untilled ground. Worth {n} unit in the compost box.
match.nPlural=other: Cut from untilled ground. Worth {n} units in the compost box.

catalog_grass_seeds: Sold in packs of {pack}. Sow on tilled soil. Roots in {seconds}s and drinks only {drink} L a day, then the plot turns back into untilled lawn.
catalog_fence: Stands in the middle of an untilled tile and joins up with any fence beside it. Boundary marker only - the gardener walks straight through.
catalog_paving: Laid on untilled ground. Keeps the garden walkable and tidy. Demolish lifts it again.
catalog_rotary_shovel: Motorised. Digs everything a Shovel digs, faster than any other shovel. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per dig.
catalog_diamond_pickaxe: Breaks rocks and very hard soil faster than any other pickaxe. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per mine.
catalog_sugar: {bag} L bag. Does not rot. Mill cane is cheaper per litre.
catalog_mill: Hopper mill. {cane} cane or {vanilla} vanilla crush in {work}s. {cane} olive crushes in {olive}s and {cane} wheat in {wheat}s.
catalog_still: Distills {cap} potato, wheat or apricot in {seconds}s.
catalog_barrel: Grapes or apples, never mixed. Five grapes or four apples fill a barrel. Wine or cider, not whisky.
catalog_jam: {fruit} fruit and sugar cook in {seconds}s. Tomato is ketchup, and San Marzano tomato is Passata, which takes no sugar.
catalog_freezer: Small {n} slots, large {m} slots. Fruit in here rots {pct}% slower. The large one is a contract prize, never sold.
catalog_furnace: Burns a mixed load into Ash. {need} units burn in {seconds}s and yield {ash} Ash. A working Furnace makes nearby machines finish faster than they do without one. A chest on the right takes the Ash, else it drops in front.
catalog_sku_buy_furnace: Burns a mixed load into Ash. {need} units burn in {seconds}s and yield {ash} Ash. Holds {cap} units. A working Furnace makes nearby machines finish faster than they do without one. A chest on the right takes the Ash, else it drops in front.
catalog_station: Studies one fruit at a time and writes down what it learns about that crop. A studied crop turns up a better Variety more often when it ripens, comes up better in seed you buy, and its stall price climbs back faster so you can sell more of it in a day. The first fruit takes {seconds}s and each one after takes longer. A plain fruit teaches one step, a named Variety two, an Heirloom three. How far a crop can go depends on how many Varieties it has.
catalog_sku_buy_research_station: Studies one fruit at a time and writes down what it learns about that crop. A studied crop turns up a better Variety more often when it ripens, comes up better in seed you buy, and its stall price climbs back faster so you can sell more of it in a day. The first fruit takes {seconds}s and each one after takes longer. A plain fruit teaches one step, a named Variety two, an Heirloom three. How far a crop can go depends on how many Varieties it has.
catalog_axe: Chops a mature tree into Wood. The tree then grows a trunk and grows again before it fruits. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per chop.
catalog_chainsaw: Chops a mature tree into Wood. Lasts for more uses and each Chop takes fewer seconds than an Axe. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per chop.
catalog_electric_chainsaw: Chops a mature tree into Wood. Lasts for more uses and each Chop takes fewer seconds than a Chainsaw. {uses} uses, {workSeconds}s per chop.
catalog_wood: Chopped from a mature tree with an Axe. Burns in a Furnace.
catalog_fly_agaric: A red mushroom flecked with white. It comes up on untilled ground around a tree, most often after rain, and turns up in Uncommon burrows. Infuse {goods} with it at an Infuser. The Compost box and the Furnace take it and the Market will not buy it, but the Necronomicon asks for three.
catalog_truffle: A dark, knobbly mushroom. It comes up on untilled ground around a tree, most often after rain, and turns up in Rare burrows. Named and Heirloom trees give a larger share of Truffles than Plain trees. Crush one at a Mill into {n} Truffle extract. The Compost box and the Furnace take it and the Market will not buy it.
catalog_truffle_extract: Crushed Truffle. Infuse {goods} with it at an Infuser.
catalog_extract: Cut grass pressed at a Mill into a {liters} L bag. Pour {pour} L on a growing plant, a sapling or a stump and it grows faster for {seconds}s, adding up to {pct}% of its growth. Use it when a plant would ripen too late for a contract. On a grown tree out of season it adds {season}% to the chance that a new season starts. A plant takes it once. Infused Extract, made at an Infuser, keeps the plant growing faster for {infused}s. The Market does not buy it.

match.nPlural=one: Left when a Furnace finishes a burn. Worth {n} unit in the Compost box.
match.nPlural=other: Left when a Furnace finishes a burn. Worth {n} units in the Compost box.

catalog_graft: Cut from a grown tree with the axe. Hold it against a young plant or a sapling to turn that plant into this variety.
catalog_infuser: Infuse {goods} in {seconds}s, and Extract in {extract}s. Each good takes one of two items, and the recipes show which. The good keeps its name, its Quality, and the money the Market pays for it, and shows a plus. Infused goods sell at Market at the percent shown for that good, and selling them does not change that percent. Finishing a contract with Infused goods raises Reputation more than the same contract without them. Infused Extract makes a plant grow faster for longer than Extract does.
catalog_sku_buy_infuser: Infuse {goods} in {seconds}s, and Extract in {extract}s. Each good takes one of two items, and the recipes show which. The good keeps its name, its Quality, and the money the Market pays for it, and shows a plus. Infused goods sell at Market at the percent shown for that good, and selling them does not change that percent. Finishing a contract with Infused goods raises Reputation more than the same contract without them. Infused Extract makes a plant grow faster for longer than Extract does.
catalog_sorter: Takes seeds and fruit in on one side and puts them out on three, sorted by Variety: Plain out the first side, Named out the second, Heirloom out the third. Empty a mixed harvest into the chest that feeds it and each of the three leaves on a side of its own. A chest on a side takes what comes out, else it drops on the ground there. Rotate it before you build to choose which way it faces.
catalog_sku_buy_sorter: Takes seeds and fruit in on one side and puts them out on three, sorted by Variety: Plain out the first side, Named out the second, Heirloom out the third. Empty a mixed harvest into the chest that feeds it and each of the three leaves on a side of its own. A chest on a side takes what comes out, else it drops on the ground there. Rotate it before you build to choose which way it faces.
catalog_flakes: Crushed Chilli. Infuse {goods} with it at an Infuser.
catalog_vanilla_extract: Crushed Vanilla. Infuse {goods} with it at an Infuser.
catalog_sku_buy_necronomicon: A book that asks for produce, for ash and for money, and pays nothing for any of it. Build it once and it stays where you put it. Each page names one thing it wants; fill a page and perform the ritual at twilight to close it.
catalog_necronomicon: The book your grandmother wrote down but never found. It sits open on the ground and takes what you carry to it, or what a chest to the west of it holds. Nothing it takes comes back.
